title: Tamsin and the Gravity
premise: Freya Almeida investigates impossible accidents on Meridian Station, a decaying colony the war has written off as a rounding error. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers it was no accident: someone used the colony's forgotten deep-space array to broadcast a peace proposal that both warring factions will kill to suppress or seize. As fleets converge and her own records reveal that the 'accidents' were cover for a decades-long conspiracy of survivors hiding in plain sight, Freya must choose between exposing the truth — which will end the war but destroy the colony's anonymity — or staying invisible while the message dies with them. She broadcasts it, at the cost of everything she protected, and the war ends not with surrender but with recognition.
about_author: Coral Thackeray is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years cataloguing disasters nobody wanted to claim. She writes science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the mathematics of survival from a houseboat off the Cornish coast.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Disasters
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She arrives at Meridian Station to investigate a cargo lift failure that killed three people and defies every actuarial model. Establishes her methodical detachment and the colony's shabby resilience. Emotional beat: professional curiosity masking a private grief she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Mid-investigation, gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds; water rises, people float, then everything settles as if nothing happened. Official channels go silent. Freya realizes her own instruments recorded something impossible: the flicker originated near Meridian. Beat: dread blooming into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, intercut with station engineer Dov Okonkwo's logs. The array beneath the colony — officially decommissioned forty years ago — drew power during the flicker. Someone here transmitted. Beat: the thrill of a pattern forming, and the first hint she is being watched.

chapters.title: The Committee of Nobody
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. He introduces Freya to the Keepers, an underground circle of colonists who have maintained the array in secret since the evacuation order was rescinded and everyone forgot Meridian existed. They didn't send the message — but they know who did. Beat: wary belonging, the warmth of being needed.

chapters.title: Accident Number Seven
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She cross-references her old case files and finds six prior 'impossible accidents' on Meridian, each one destroying evidence of the array's activity. The deaths weren't random; they were erasures. Beat: cold fury, the investigator realizing she has been investigating a cover-up all along.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Static
chapters.summary: Keeper archivist Mirela Senn's POV. She plays the fragmentary transmission recovered from the flicker: a peace proposal authored by a long-dead colonial governor, addressed to both warring factions, offering proof of a shared crime that started the war. Beat: awe and terror — the message is real, and it damns everyone.

chapters.title: Visitors
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. An insurance 'audit team' arrives — clearly military intelligence in civilian clothes, led by the urbane Casimir Voss. They know about the flicker and want the array's records. Freya lies for the first time in her career. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying Hidden
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. The Keepers debate: destroy the array and stay invisible forever, or finish the transmission and become a target. Old wounds surface — families lost to earlier purges. Dov argues for silence; his daughter disagrees. Beat: love strained against survival instinct.

chapters.title: Paper Trails
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She reconstructs the original crime the message exposes: the war's opening atrocity was staged by both governments jointly, to justify the war itself. Her own employer helped bury the evidence. Beat: vertigo — her entire professional life built atop a lie.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Voss privately offers her extraction, wealth, and amnesty if she hands over the transmission coordinates. He reveals he knows about her brother, lost in the war's first year — the grief she's been outrunning. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: What My Brother Would Have Done
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, intimate and interior. She reads her brother's last letters and finds he served under a commander later implicated in the staged atrocity. The message isn't abstract anymore; it's his unfinished sentence. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. The array's power core is sabotaged; two Keepers die in a fire that mirrors Accident Number Seven exactly. Voss's team denies involvement — someone else wants the message dead too. Beat: mourning, paranoia, the enemy multiplying.

chapters.title: Three Fleets
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Long-range sensors show three battle groups converging on Meridian: both warring factions and a third, unidentified flotilla. Estimated arrival: eleven days. The colony's invisibility is over whether they like it or not. Beat: claustrophobic countdown begins.

chapters.title: The Repair
chapters.summary: Freya and Dov's alternating POV. A grueling EVA sequence to rebuild the core by hand, Freya learning the physical labor of hope while Dov teaches her the array's history — how the Keepers kept faith when no one asked them to. Beat: trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Roster
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cross-referencing casualty lists, she identifies the saboteur: a Keeper planted years ago by her own insurance syndicate, reporting on the array all along. Confrontation is quiet and devastating. Beat: betrayal without villainy — just fear wearing loyalty's face.

chapters.title: Voss Returns
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. With fleets inbound, Voss drops the pretense: his faction will glass the colony rather than let the message land. He offers one last deal — give him the message and he'll evacuate the colonists. Some of them. Beat: the price of survival made explicit and unbearable.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Full ensemble scene, Mirela presiding. The Keepers and colonists vote openly for the first time in forty years: broadcast, negotiate, or hide. Freya speaks last, laying out the truth including her own complicity. Beat: democracy as an act of courage; the vote to transmit carries.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Freya and Dov's POV. The transmission sequence runs while Voss's strike team breaches the station. Firefights in the corridors, Mirela holding the console, the array charging. Beat: white-knuckle climax, sacrifice stacked on sacrifice.

chapters.title: Everything We Were Hiding
chapters.summary: Climax. The message goes out — full, unredacted, to every ship in the system. The third fleet is revealed: neutral arbiters who have waited decades for jurisdictional grounds to intervene. Voss's faction stands down under threat of universal exposure. Beat: catharsis through truth-telling.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Actuarial
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She files her final report: not an insurance document but testimony, naming every erased accident and every erased person. The syndicate collapses; investigations begin. Beat: quiet reckoning, grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Gravity, Steady
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Weeks later, supply ships arrive — Meridian is remembered now, mapped, claimed, changed forever. The Keepers disband, their secrecy obsolete. Dov watches his daughter board a ship for school on a world she'd only seen in archives. Beat: bittersweet cost of visibility.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Gravity
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. She learns the message's author signed it with a pseudonym — Tamsin — and that the nine-second flicker was the array's farewell handshake, gravity briefly acknowledging its maker. Standing on the observation deck as new colonies light up around her, Freya finally belongs to a story larger than her losses. Beat: peace earned, identity chosen.
